concerns.concern: The edge signature is a narrow peak near the Fermi level. A helical 1D Dirac edge should instead give a roughly constant, edge-enhanced density of states across the whole bulk gap. The authors must explain why a peak is expected and where the computed edge Dirac point lies.
concerns.quote: The authors must explain quantitatively why a peak, rather than a plateau, is expected, and where in energy the DFT edge Dirac point lies relative to the measured gap.

concerns.concern: Edge spectra were taken only over ±100 mV. No edge-versus-center comparison spans the full ~300 meV gap and the band edges, so the gap-wide behaviour of the edge state is untested.
concerns.quote: Spectra were acquired only over ±100 mV with V_stab = −0.1 V. No edge-versus-center comparison spanning the full gap (and the band edges) is shown.

concerns.concern: The edge peak sits only ~10 meV above the valence-band maximum, at the bottom of the gap. It could therefore come from trivial causes such as edge band bending, edge-localized valence states or dangling bonds, none of which are excluded.
concerns.quote: At such an energy, the peak can easily arise from trivial causes

concerns.concern: A feature pinned exactly at zero bias may be a zero-bias anomaly, such as Coulomb blockade, a Kondo-like resonance or a tip artefact. Temperature- and setpoint-dependent spectra are needed to rule these out.
concerns.quote: Features pinned exactly at zero bias are notoriously susceptible to zero-bias anomalies

concerns.concern: There is no trivial-phase control. Edges of Si₂Te₂ on Sb₂Te₃ should be measured with identical parameters to show that the Fermi-level peak is absent there.
concerns.quote: No trivial-phase control. The authors' own Si₂Te₂/Sb₂Te₃ system (trivial) is the ideal reference

concerns.concern: The islands are only ~8–10 nm across, so edge states decaying over 2–3 nm could hybridize across the island and open a finite-size gap. Confinement and charging effects are also not discussed. Measurements on much larger islands are needed.
concerns.quote: The islands are small (~8–10 nm across, Fig. 5a,d).

concerns.concern: A 2–3 nm spatial extent does not rule out trivial edge mechanisms. Band bending, electrostatic edge potentials or trivial edge states can decay over similar lengths.
concerns.quote: The argument that a 2–3 nm width "rules out" defects or dangling bonds is weak.

concerns.concern: If HfTe₂ states lie inside the Si₂Te₂ gap, the heterostructure is metallic. The edge states could then hybridize with the substrate continuum, which undermines topological protection. Edge-state lifetime and broadening should be discussed.
concerns.quote: the helical edge states can hybridize with the substrate continuum. The protection against backscattering, invoked as motivation, would be compromised.

concerns.concern: Only one dI/dV map, at +7 mV, is shown. It was taken in constant-current mode at a step edge, where topographic cross-talk is strong. Maps at several in-gap and band-edge energies, plus constant-height or normalized maps, are needed.
concerns.quote: Only one dI/dV map at +7 mV is shown (Fig. 5e). It was taken with V_stab = 0.2 V in constant-current mode

concerns.concern: There is no test of helicity or suppressed backscattering, such as QPI near edges, spin-polarized STM or magnetic-field measurements.
concerns.quote: There are no QPI or backscattering-suppression measurements near the edge, no magnetic-field or spin-polarized STM tests of helicity

concerns.concern: For a metallic heterostructure, the Z₂ calculation via Wannier charge centers does not specify which occupied bands are used, or whether they are separated by a direct gap at every k-point.
concerns.quote: requires a clearly specified set of occupied bands, isolated by a direct gap at every k-point. This is not specified.

concerns.concern: The gap nearly doubles, from 220 to 429 meV, despite weak vdW coupling, and the two values come from different functionals. This may be a functional artefact. A same-functional comparison and tests of robustness against functional choice and interlayer distance are needed.
concerns.quote: It is surprising that a weak vdW interaction (−0.296 eV per cell) nearly doubles the gap... This may simply be a functional artefact.

concerns.concern: A commensurate (1×1) overlayer on HfTe₂ (a ≈ 395–396 pm) contradicts the strain-free claim. Either the Si₂Te₂ is strained, or the overlayer is incommensurate and a moiré should be visible.
concerns.quote: Hence either the Si₂Te₂ is tensile-strained, or the overlayer is incommensurate.

concerns.concern: Distinguishing 390 from 396 pm requires lattice calibration better than 1%, which is not documented. This matters because topology survives only in a narrow strain window.
concerns.quote: Distinguishing 390 pm from 396 pm (≈1.5%) requires calibration better than 1%... This is not documented.

concerns.concern: No chemical probe confirms composition. Alternative phases (Te adlayers, Si₂Te₃-like phases, Si–Hf intermixing, Te-deficient HfTe₂) are not excluded, and XPS/AES, LEED or ARPES are needed.
concerns.quote: Without composition data, identification of the Te–Si–Si–Te structure rests on lattice constant and step height alone.

concerns.concern: The "experimental" gap Eg′ = 319 meV appears to be defined using the HfTe₂ valence-band maximum. It is unclear why a substrate band edge should define the gap measured on the Si₂Te₂ island.
concerns.quote: it is not clear why a substrate band edge should define the "observed" gap.

concerns.concern: Invoking a rigid 0.25 eV shift while claiming close agreement between the 300 and 319 meV gaps is inconsistent. The authors should state which experimental band edges correspond to which DFT bands, within one consistent band-alignment picture.
concerns.quote: It is then inconsistent to claim close quantitative agreement between a 300 meV and a 319 meV gap

concerns.concern: The measured gap has nonzero in-gap signal and smeared band edges, and the edges are assigned from a single spectrum. Error bars, statistics over the 20 islands and an explicit edge-definition criterion are needed.
concerns.quote: The dI/dV signal in the gap is clearly nonzero, and the band edges are "smeared".

concerns.concern: The V-shaped dip around zero bias in the island-center spectrum is unexplained, given that the bulk gap is ~300 meV wide. It hints at a zero-bias anomaly.
concerns.quote: The "V-shaped dip between ±50 mV" (or ±10 mV) in the island-center spectrum is itself unexplained

concerns.concern: The small peak attributed to substrate-induced states further complicates interpretation of the spectra.
concerns.quote: The "small peak … attributed to substrate-induced states" further complicates interpretation.

concerns.concern: The claim that the edge state is independent of step geometry is not established. There is no systematic comparison of edge orientations or terminations, and no assessment near defects or kinks.
concerns.quote: "Independent of step geometry" is not established.

concerns.concern: The edge ring in the conductance map is inhomogeneous, and the missing segment on one edge is attributed to tip effects without evidence.
concerns.quote: the missing segment on the lower edge is attributed to "tip effects" without evidence.

concerns.concern: In the commensurate DFT cell, Si₂Te₂ keeping 389 pm is a model constraint, not a result. The strain imposed on HfTe₂ and its effect on the HfTe₂ bands and band alignment should be reported.
concerns.quote: The statement that Si₂Te₂ "remains at 389 pm" after relaxation is therefore a constraint of the model rather than a result.

concerns.concern: The DFT model uses only monolayer HfTe₂, while the experimental substrate is bulk. A multilayer or bulk-like slab should be used.
concerns.quote: Use a model with a multilayer or bulk-like HfTe₂ slab, rather than only ML-HfTe₂

concerns.concern: The measured step height (710 pm) differs by ~10% from the calculated value (790 pm), and the bias dependence of the apparent height is not shown.
concerns.quote: The measured step height (710 pm) differs by ~10% from the calculated interlayer spacing (790 pm). Bias dependence of the apparent height is not shown.

concerns.concern: Claims about room-temperature QSH behaviour are speculative, because all data were taken at 5.8 K.
concerns.quote: All data are at 5.8 K, so claims about room-temperature QSH physics are speculative.

concerns.concern: The reference cited for the WCC-based Z₂ method (Giustino & Pasquarello) is inappropriate. Soluyanov & Vanderbilt or Yu et al. should be cited instead.
concerns.quote: The cited Ref. 39 (Giustino & Pasquarello, mixed Wannier–Bloch functions) is not the appropriate reference for WCC-based Z₂ evaluation

concerns.concern: The number of screened candidates is inconsistent between Fig. 1(a) (65) and the text (76).
concerns.quote: the number of candidates: 65 in Fig. 1(a) versus 76 in the text

concerns.concern: The description of the Supplementary Material in Ref. 35 mentions "three stripe orientations" and appears copy-pasted from elsewhere.
concerns.quote: the description of the SM in Ref. 35, which refers to "three stripe orientations" and appears copy-pasted

concerns.concern: There are typographical errors such as "remains challenge", "deriving the system" and "valance".
concerns.quote: typographical errors such as "remains challenge", "deriving the system", "valance".
